newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-FORMER HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION BOWE ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-FORMER HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION BOWE ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT.

text.p: Former world heavyweight boxing champion Riddick Bowe, who earlier this year quit the Marines, said Wednesday he is quitting the ring.

Bowe, who struggled in his last two bouts against Andrew Golota before winning both when his Polish-born opponent was disqualified for low blows, said he was leaving the ring to become part of a community service programme by Home Box Office television called "Reaching Beyond the Ring."
"Although my time inside the ring has come to an end, it's just the start of an exciting and important career for me," Bowe said.
The programme was established in 1995 to serve as a vehicle for HBO boxers and boxing announcers to participate in charitable and community programmes.
The 29-year-old Bowe compiled a record of 40-1-1 with 32 knockouts. He last fought on December 14, when he was awarded a win by disqualification over Golota.

Bowe, who often allowed his weight to balloon between fights, joined the United States Marines earlier this year, saying he was fulfilling a childhood dream. But Bowe was discharged just 11 days after arriving at a Marine Corps' boot camp in Parris Island, South Carolina.
Bowe defeated Evander Holyfield in November 1992 to capture the undisputed world heavyweight title.

He gave up the World Boxing Council belt following a dispute, then lost the World Boxing Association and International Boxing Federation heavyweight versions of the title to Holyfield in November 1993.
Bowe rallied to knock out Holyfield in a non-title bout on November 4, 1995.
A native of Brooklyn, Bowe won four New York Golden Glove titles and won a silver medal at the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul before turning professional on March 6, 1989.
Bowe has long been active in community service, receiving honours over the years for civic achievements.

In 1993, Bowe flew to Somalia to donate $1 million in food and supplies to starving people and was subsequently honoured by South African president Nelson Mandela and received a blessing from Pope John Paul II for his efforts.
